title: Cooking Gluten‑Free Falafel on a Stainless Steel Gyro Pan
meta_description: Master gluten free falafel using a vertical gyro pan. Learn how to stack, roast, and slice a gluten-free falafel tower for the perfect home gyro.
html:
Most people think of falafel as something you deep-fry in batches, leaving you with a greasy mess and a kitchen that smells like a chippy for three days. But if you have a vertical gyro pan, you can flip the script. By stacking gluten-free falafel patties into a tower, you get a roasting effect that mimics the traditional shawarma rotisserie, resulting in a crisp exterior and a moist, herb-filled center.

Using a gluten free falafel gyro pan setup allows you to cook a large batch at once while letting the excess oil drip away from the meat or vegetable patties. Here is how to master this technique using the Vertical Gyro Pan with Skewer for Oven.

Preparing Your Gluten-Free Falafel Base

The biggest challenge with gluten-free falafel is stability. Traditional falafel uses chickpeas, but without gluten or a heavy binder, the patties can crumble when stacked on a skewer. To ensure your tower stays intact, use a blend of soaked (but not overcooked) chickpeas and a small amount of chickpea flour or a gluten-free all-purpose flour blend.

Pulse your ingredients in a food processor until coarse—not a smooth paste. You want texture. Fold in plenty of fresh parsley, cilantro, garlic, and cumin. To make these "gyro-ready," form the mixture into thick, uniform discs about one inch thick. Chill these discs in the refrigerator for at least an hour before assembling; this firms up the starches and prevents the tower from sliding down the skewer.

Assembling the Tower in the Vertical Gyro Pan

Now comes the fun part. The Vertical Gyro Pan with Skewer for Oven is designed for rotating meats, but it works beautifully for vegetable-based stacks. Start by placing the pan on the oven rack and inserting the vertical skewer.

Slide your chilled gluten-free falafel discs onto the skewer one by one. Press them down firmly to eliminate air gaps. The tighter the stack, the more heat is conducted through the center of the tower, ensuring the middle patties cook at the same rate as the edges. If you're worried about the top patty sliding, you can secure it with a slice of onion or a thick piece of bell pepper to act as a "cap."

Roasting Your Gluten-Free Falafel Gyro Pan Setup

Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C). Brush the exterior of your falafel tower generously with olive oil. This is crucial because the vertical roasting method relies on convection; the oil helps the heat penetrate the patties and creates that signature golden-brown crust.

Slide the stainless steel vertical skewer pan into the center of the oven. Roast for approximately 25 to 35 minutes. Depending on the thickness of your patties, you may want to carefully rotate the pan 90 degrees halfway through if your oven has "hot spots." Because the pan is stainless steel, it distributes heat efficiently, and the drip tray catches any oil, keeping your oven floor clean.

Slicing and Serving the Perfect Gyro

Once the edges are crisp and deep brown, remove the pan from the oven. Let the tower rest for 5 minutes. This allows the proteins to set, ensuring you get clean slices rather than crumbled pieces.

Using a sharp carving knife, shave the falafel off the skewer in thin, vertical strips. This mimics the experience of a professional gyro shop. To build your platter or wrap, follow this assembly order for the best texture:

  • Base: A warmed gluten-free pita or a bed of crisp romaine lettuce.
  • Protein: A generous heap of the shaved gluten-free falafel.
  • Freshness: Diced cucumbers, cherry tomatoes, and pickled red onions.
  • Sauce: A heavy drizzle of lemon-tahini sauce or a garlic tzatziki.

Cleaning Your Stainless Steel Gyro Pan

One of the best parts of using a stainless steel vertical skewer pan for oven-roasted gyros is the durability. Because it's high-grade stainless steel, you don't have to worry about the warping that happens with cheaper aluminum pans.

After cooking, let the pan cool slightly, then soak it in warm, soapy water. If any falafel bits are stuck to the skewer, a nylon scrub brush will take them right off without scratching the surface. For a deep clean, these pans are typically dishwasher safe, making the cleanup almost as easy as the cooking process.

FAQ

Can I add vegetables between the falafel layers?

Yes! Adding slices of zucchini, red onion, or red bell pepper between the falafel discs adds moisture and flavor. Just ensure the vegetables are sliced to the same thickness as the falafel to keep the tower stable.

Will the falafel fall off the skewer during cooking?

As long as you chill the patties before stacking and press them firmly together, they should stay put. The heat causes the starches to bind, effectively "locking" the tower together as it roasts.

Can I use this method for other gluten-free appetizers?

Absolutely. This vertical roasting technique works great for gluten-free halloumi cheese stacks or marinated tofu blocks. Anything that can be formed into a disc and stacked will benefit from the vertical heat distribution of the gyro pan.
